newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/No big rush to puts on decline.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/No big rush to puts on decline.

text.p: U.S. stocks posted sharp declines Monday but traders said investors were not rushing to buy puts for protection.
"The market's definitely going to go down 100 points but there's no big put buying," said Harrison Roth, a first vice president at Cowen & Co.
In afternoon action, the bellwether Dow industrial average was down 99 points at 7,697 after hitting a new session low at about 7,691.
Dealers said trading in most major U.S. index options was on the quiet side after Friday's hectic expiration.

"People are winding down from the expiration," one trader said. "A lot of option traders tend to take off after the expiration or take a deep breath and start to look at setting up new positions for the upcoming month."
At the Chicago Board Options Exchange, put volume outpaced call volume by nearly two to one in the S&P 500 index .SPX.
SPX put volume at 1400 CDT/1900 GMT was 32,216 compared to call volume of 16,755.
The spot SPX index was down 12.58 at 886.12 and September S&P 500 futures fell 13.85 to 891.
The S&P 100 index, was off 12.62 at 863.85.
Among OEX options, put volume topped call volume by 22,368 to 17,630.
Traders said the selling pressure extended to OEX options, where the CBOE's volatility index rose 0.83, or 3.7 percent, to 23.27 by late trading.
The VIX is calculated off certain OEX options.
OEX options activity was led by the July 830 puts, which traded 4,380 contracts. The July 800 put traded 2,440 and the July 870 put traded 2,320.
The busiest OEX call was the July 870, with 2,260.
In the SPX, trading was led by the 7,105 July 870 puts that traded. The next most active put was the July 860, with turnover of about 2,510.
On the call side, activity was led by the July 900, the July 975 and the July 925.
